edits.add_before: | `ops-review-d945278/*.json` | Spent 2026-08-24, `--no-approval` disclosed (repairs the commit it reviews; no second reviewer was available). **Discharges the adversarial review of `d945278` — 3 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, every one CONFIRMED by execution.** The two High findings are one defect twice: the file-guard allowlist `return`ed before all thirteen category branches, so a `tests/`/`fixtures/` path component was not a certificate exemption but a blanket one — `tests/fixtures/.env`, `test/secrets.json`, `tests/id_rsa`, `testdata/wallet.dat`, `spec/fixtures/terraform.tfstate`, `home/tests/.aws/credentials`, `k8s/tests/secret-db.yaml` and five `pii/`/dump shapes all lost their flag — and the differential gate written in the same commit reported OK, because **its corpus contained no non-certificate secret under a test component: it was drawn from the widening it was meant to police.** Once that commit reached `origin/main`, `--baseline auto` would have resolved to a merge-base containing the allowlist, so the blindness was permanent, not a one-run miss. Fixes: the allowlist is nested inside `case "${basename##*.}" in cert|crt|pem|key|p12|pfx|pub)` so it is unreachable for any other extension; `pii/` and `production/*data*` became unconditional (the schema/model exclusion had been conjoined ahead of all three predicates, freeing `pii/model_training_data.csv`); 19 corpus paths added, one per category under a test component. Also: `O_TRUNC` truncated the lock file on OPEN, i.e. before the flock, so a REFUSED contender destroyed the holder's pid in the one case it exists for (now `ftruncate` after acquisition, mode `0600`); the refusal message told operators to "remove the lock file if stale", which reopens the race now that a leftover file is normal; the reversed e2e assertion was `if lock.exists(): assert ...` — guarded by the very property it should assert, so restoring the unlink left it green; the parse gate matched only ```` ```bash ````, so ```` ```sh ```` and ```` ``` bash ```` evaded it; and `log() { hlog "$@"; }` broke the graceful degradation its own `[ -f lib.sh ] &&` guard promises. **The lesson: every one of these is 'I proved the property I was thinking about, not the property that mattered.' Four mutation proofs of mine missed what one adversarial reader found in eight minutes.** Plan: `plan-review-d945278.md`. |
